bindings.label: A 17-year-old female had a 7-month history of intermittent lower extremity swelling, proteinuria, and hematuria.

A renal biopsy at another hospital 4 months prior suggested possible IgA nephropathy, and she was treated with the angiotensin receptor blocker valsartan but symptoms persisted; she had no history of drug use, infections, malignancy, or family history of hepatitis B or C, HIV, rheumatic disease, or tumors; she was normotensive, and both general physical and funduscopic examinations were normal; her lung fields were clear without rales or fremitus.

A 24-hour urine protein test showed a total protein level of 2.75 g; urinalysis revealed 24 erythrocytes per high-power field; serum levels of urea, creatinine, and albumin were within normal ranges; autoantibody tests were unremarkable, and serum antiphospholipase A2 receptor antibodies were negative; renal ultrasound findings were normal.

A review of the previous renal biopsy showed 22 glomeruli, with 1 (4.5%) showing global sclerosis and 1 (4.5%) showing focal segmental sclerosis; there was mild mesangial expansion, thickening of the glomerular basement membrane, endothelial swelling, focally swollen podocytes, and hypercellularity; swelling of the tubular epithelium and patchy infiltration of lymphocytes and monocytes in the interstitial area were noted, without interstitial fibrosis; the capillary walls in the interstitial area showed no lesions.

Immunohistochemical analysis revealed granular deposits along the capillary walls for IgM, C3, C1q, and kappa and lambda light chains, with mild staining for IgG and IgA; IgG subclass staining showed segmental positivity for IgG1 but negativity for IgG2, IgG3, IgG4, and antiphospholipase A2 receptor; granular deposits along the capillary walls, especially for lambda and C1q, indicated immune complexes; silver staining showed spike-like projections at the 3-o'clock position, indicating a spiked glomerular basement membrane around the immune complexes; Masson staining showed scattered fuchsinophilic deposits, indicating immune complexes; lesions of mesangial cells, endothelial cells, and podocytes were noted.

Lupus nephritis was excluded due to the absence of systemic lupus manifestations and negative immunoserological markers except for an antinuclear antibody titer of 1:100; no solid tumors or hematological malignancies were detected by computed tomography or hematological examinations, and all tumor biomarkers were negative.
